title: Exercise: Ask the following questions
use_cases: Use when drafting initial profiles for main characters in a narrative
Implement when building a comprehensive character backstory to ensure consistency
Configure when defining character speech patterns and dialogue style
Use when analyzing a character's internal motivations and external fears
Use when establishing a character's social hierarchy and family history
content:
Ask these questions for each main character. Feel free to add more. This is just the starting point:

1. How does he say hello?
2. What is your character’s style of speech?
3. What is the sound of your character’s voice?
4. What is your character’s disposition?
5. What are his morals and beliefs?
6. Is he or she educated? How far?
7. How old are they?
8. How would the character be described physically by a stranger (include height, weight, ethnicity)?
9. Where are they from?
10. Has he lived there all of his life or has he moved?
11. Who are their parents and what is their relationship with them like?
12. Does your character look more like mom or dad?
13. Does your character have siblings?
14. Are they close to their siblings? Why or why not?
15. What was the character’s childhood like?
16. What is your character’s greatest success?
17. What is your character’s greatest failure?
18. How is your character’s outlook on life? In general, is he pessimistic? Optimistic?
19. What are the three most important motivations for the character?
20. What are the three most important fears for the character?
21. What is your character’s profession? Is he or she a student?
22. Are they happy or not with their profession? Why?
23. What is your character’s hobby? What does he or she do for fun?
24. Who are/ were his best friends?
25. Does your character have a lot of friends?
26. Does your character have any enemies?
27. Is your character married? Dating? Why?
28. What do they want from a relationship?
29. Does he have any children?
30. Who is the most significant person in your character’s life?
31. What makes your character happy?
32. What makes your character sad?
33. What is the most important, defining event in your character’s life?
34. Is your character predominantly passive or aggressive?
35. Is he or she introverted or extroverted?
